title: Saturday evening
suits: consumer, local, leisure, travel, social and transit products; warm pitches about people. Walk data-tod forward for a sunset across the deck.

params.data-tod: 0 late afternoon (5 pm) · .5 sunset · 1 blue hour; any value in between
params.--brand: on the section: the kite, the tour boat's flag, one moored dinghy
params.--brand-2: on the section: the kite's second panel, every fourth ferris-wheel cabin
params.--field (set by the scene): the sky behind the headline zone, so --ink-auto stays right

details: a steam train crosses left to right on a brick viaduct every 52 s; its chimney puffs in choo-choo pairs, with faint wisps between so the plume stays one plume
the steam leaves with the train's momentum, stops, rises, drifts left with the wind and thins as it grows
low white wisps hiss from the cylinder cocks at the front wheels on every first chuff
the driver toots once mid-crossing: a thin, fast white jet from the whistle by the cab
coupling and connecting rods turn with the wheels; the firebox under the cab flickers orange
after dark the firebox lights the underside of fresh steam orange; the coaches' windows glow and show heads
a semaphore signal drops to clear with a little bounce 8 s before the train appears and returns after the last coach
two birds on the telegraph wire take off as the loco nears, loop, and settle back after the train has gone
a skateboarder rolls along the far promenade and ollies once every 40 s, board tilting nose-up
a second skater kick-pushes in threes, surging on each push, then rides
a walker carries a board under one arm; a dog trots ahead of its owner, tail wagging, leash sagging
a cyclist pedals past; at dusk the rear light blinks and the front lamp is on
a red-and-amber kite bobs on the wind, tail streaming left, its line sagging to the flyer's raised hand; after dark the kite has gone home
birds head home in a loose V, flapping then gliding, shrinking as they descend into the promenade trees; after dark two bats flit by the lamps instead
a tiny ferris wheel on the right edge turns once every two minutes, cabins hanging level; its rim lights come on at sunset
windows light up one by one as the hour deepens (same windows, same order on every slide); a few west-facing panes flash with the low sun at 5 pm
one window flickers TV blue, one lights late (someone just got home), one goes dark for a while
street lamps come on after sunset; the next one to come on warms up sodium-pink with a stutter; one lamp is faulty and blinks
the clock tower shows the hour of the light: 5:00 in the afternoon, about twenty to eight at sunset, ten to nine at blue hour
a red aircraft light blinks on the TV tower once the light goes
the far bank is mirrored in the river, squashed and rippled, and lit windows smear into the water at night
the sun's glitter path on the river, sky glints drifting downstream with the current, lamp glints quivering under each lamp
a festooned tour boat chugs upstream with its flag streaming back; a sculler goes downstream surging on each stroke and leaving little oar puddles that fade
moored dinghies by the river steps nod against the wall, out of step with each other
one wind everywhere: steam, kite tail, flag and clouds all go right to left
a thin waxing crescent at blue hour, lit on the side facing where the sun went down; the city's own warm glow on the low sky
